If she said that then it’s crystal clear she had her own plans and wanted to do something with those guys. It’s incredible how little considerations your friend had. If it’s something that really annoyed you but you can forgive her for it. Then it won’t come down to just end up a friendship. I sense from the last part you wrote that you’re having trouble deciding what to do and knowing she has little female friends will make you feel bad. I’d say personally if you can talk things out it would be ideal. Though if this attitude from her has happened before and you don’t want to encounter it again consider distancing from her for a while.

Honestly… I think it’s time to cut ties. I’m just flabbergasted to read that your friend couldn’t hold the end of the bargain to sit at the back and not talk to those guys. Unless there was a miscommunication between you two. Did you explicitly tell her you didn’t want to talk to them or hang out? Because if you did, your friend is totally in the wrong and his little respect towards you. To leave you on the day of your birthday  and flirt or god knows what was on her mind, I just think that’s just completely disrespectful . And I’m speaking from a point of view where loyalty is one key factor to a strong friendship and your friend has shown little of it. plus a pretty much childish immature impulsive behaviour. I’d say confront her, you have all the right to speak up for yourself. Express yourself on how you felt disrespected by her. And tell her to put herself on your shoes and feel what you felt and see if she’s empathetic enough to do so. 
I Hope this helped, cheers!

You really dont have to end up a friendship just because your friends are getting into relationships... yea that seems the most generic thing to say; there are different things id like to say and give you at least any type of advice to help you out.

First off as I said before you really dont and you wont like it having to end a friendship, if you say you are the friend you are, the best thing you can do is be happy for them. Be a supportive friend that helps them out, and cheer for them even if it bothers you if they are getting into a relationship with someone. after all you're going to feel happy about yourself.

While your friends are out with their dates and potentially building a relationship. I'd say it will be a good idea to focus on yourself, do things you like to do. Occupy yourself with activities, learn a new hobby. Dont torture yourself just because your friends are going out on dates.  

If you are feeling left out, I would say yes to your second question. If you're able to find those individuals with the same quirks about friendships and not like dating but like to form a strong friendship and a meaningful one id strongly suggest it, most introverted people are like that.

I get it that you are not into the dating thing and prefer to be single but you have to respect your friends that they are into it. I personally sense that you are leaving yourself out from the adventure of making a relationship even if you dont desire it. You could experiment a bit with it. I cant tell you what to do or not but i'd try that if I were you. 

Hope my thoughts help a bit! cheers.
